{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review — Master Services Agreement (Vendor form)
**Status:** For negotiation

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The liability, insurance, warranty, audit, assignment and renewal architecture is strong and needs no redlining — several provisions (mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims, cyber cover of USD 5,000,000, CPI-capped renewal uplift, missed-reminder extension) meet or exceed our preferred positions.

The difficulties are concentrated in two areas. First, there is a genuine drafting gap: **there is no indemnification clause at all**. The body runs from § 19.5 directly to § 21, with no Section 20, even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to indemnity obligations that do not exist. As drafted we would fund our own defence of third-party IP claims. We have inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position, numbering the remedies subsection 20.5 so the existing § 9.3 cross-reference resolves.

Second, a cluster of clauses imposes one-sided restraints on us that are internally inconsistent with the Agreement's own § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made **no** exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. Those clauses are §§ 2.1 (three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights), 7.2 (disclose-and-match), 12.4 (24-month non-compete) and 12.4 (24-month no-hire). Each sits in walk-away territory on our playbook. We also have no termination for convenience against a three-year locked term, no transition-assistance or data-return obligation, Vendor ownership of every Deliverable under a revocable term-limited licence, and a Singapore governing law clause in § 28.1 that contradicts the New York jurisdiction clause in § 28.2.

We note one procedural point: the governing law finding did not clear our verification step and should be re-confirmed against the execution copy before it is put to Vendor.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3, 9.2) |
| 3 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 (with §§ 7.3, 22.2) |
| 4 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) |
| 5 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) |
| 6 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 10.2 (gap; new § 10.3 proposed) |
| 7 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) |
| 8 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| 9 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** *(verification failed — re-confirm)* | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) |
| 10 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No Section 20 (gap between §§ 19.5 and 21) |
| 11 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |
| 12 | Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 |
| 13 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 14.2 (§§ 13.1–13.3 compliant) |
| 14 | Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| 15 | Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | **Deviation** | § 2.1 |
| 16 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| 17 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| 18 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9.3 (gap; new § 9.4 proposed) |

### 2.1 Notes on the deviations and gaps

**§ 2.1 — Minimum commitment (MINCOMMIT).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights" is walk-away territory and falls short of our fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 and with the Order Form fee structure in § 7.1. We have replaced it with pay-for-what-is-ordered-or-used, and offered the fallback in comment.

**§ 7.2 — Disclose-and-match (EXCLUSIVITY and MFN).** This single provision breaches two rules independently: as a sourcing restraint it is a de facto right of first refusal with no category limit, no 12-month sunset and no performance-failure exit; as an MFN it runs the wrong way, obliging us to extend Vendor any better third-party terms with no comparability carve-outs. Both fail the respective fallbacks and both contradict § 12.3. Our redline deletes the obligation and confirms Vendor's non-exclusive status.

**§ 12.4 — Non-compete (NONCOMPETE).** A 24-month post-term restraint on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," with no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Deletion is the minimal fix and restores consistency with § 12.3.

**§ 12.4 — No-hire (NOSOLICIT).** This is a no-hire rather than a non-solicit, covering all Vendor employees for the term plus 24 months "regardless of how the employee applies." We have narrowed it to our fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. Outright deletion remains acceptable to us.

**No Section 20 — Indemnification (INDEMN).** No indemnity exists anywhere; the contiguous numbering confirms a drafting gap rather than an extraction error. We have inserted a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, extended to Customer Affiliates, with customary IP exclusions, a notice/control/cooperation procedure with a no-adverse-settlement carve-out, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at § 20.5, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. No super-cap was added because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the cap — better than our fallback.

**§ 14.2 — Deliverable ownership and licence (IP and LICENSE).** Vendor owns every Deliverable created specifically for us, and our licence is revocable, non-transferable and limited to the Order Form term. This fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense). The § 13.2 perpetual licence does not cure it — that covers Vendor Technology and embedded paid-up software, not the Deliverable. Our redline flips assignment to us while preserving Vendor Technology under § 14.3, and conforms the licence terms to §§ 13.1–13.3 (Affiliates and contractors, revocation only for uncured material breach).

**New § 9.4 — Termination for convenience (T4C).** Section 9 offers cause-based exits only, against a three-year term and a take-or-pay commitment with no termination right. We have added a Customer-only right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly overriding the § 2.1 no-termination language for the terminated Services. Vendor has no convenience right, which is acceptable to us.

**New § 10.3 — Transition and data return (TRANSITION).** Section 10 covers only loss of access, Deliverable delivery and refunds; § 16.5 defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 covers only processing purpose and privacy compliance. We have inserted up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with backup and legal-retention carve-outs mirroring § 16.5.

**§ 28.1 — Governing law (GOVLAW).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside our accepted list and contradicts § 28.2, which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. Our redline conforms § 28.1 to New York law and New York County courts. **This finding did not pass verification and must be re-checked against the execution copy before it is raised.** The § 28.3 pre-suit executive escalation is acceptable process and is not flagged.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (no Section 20).** Absence of any IP indemnity is walk-away. Non-negotiable in substance, though we are flexible on drafting.
2. **§ 2.1 — three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Multi-year take-or-pay without an exit is walk-away; we require at minimum the 12-month reducible/true-up fallback.
3. **§ 7.2 — open-ended disclose-and-match.** Walk-away as both exclusive dealing and an open-ended MFN against us.
4. **§ 12.4 — 24-month, all-territory, undefined-scope non-compete.** Walk-away; deletion sought.
5. **§ 12.4 — no-hire covering all Vendor employees for term plus 24 months.** Walk-away; the 12-month mutual non-solicit fallback is the floor.
6. **§ 14.2 — revocable, non-transferable, term-limited Deliverable licence.** Walk-away; we need at minimum the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free fallback.
7. **No termination for convenience against a three-year locked term.** Walk-away as combined with § 2.1.
8. **§ 28.1 — exclusive Singapore law and venue.** Walk-away as an exclusive foreign forum, subject to the verification point above.

We would highlight to Vendor that items 2, 3, 4 and 5 all contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3. That inconsistency is our strongest lever and suggests these provisions may be template residue rather than a negotiated position.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify § 28.1** against the execution copy before circulating; the governing law finding failed verification and the apparent § 28.1 / § 28.2 conflict should be confirmed on the face of the document.
2. **Issue the redline** covering: new Section 20 (indemnity, remedies at 20.5); new § 9.4 (termination for convenience); new § 10.3 (transition and data return); revised § 2.1 (pay for what is ordered or used); deletion of the § 7.2 disclose-and-match; deletion of the § 12.4 non-compete; narrowing of the § 12.4 no-hire; and revision of § 14.2 (ownership and licence).
3. **Flag the duplicate numbering** to Vendor — there are two provisions numbered 7.2 and two numbered 12.4, and no Section 11 or Section 20 — and ask Vendor to confirm the intended structure so cross-references (§§ 9.3, 16.5, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) resolve.
4. **Brief the business owner** on the § 2.1 commitment and the absence of any convenience exit, so we understand the commercial appetite before we concede on either.
5. **Confirm no further trading** on the compliant provisions (liability cap, assignment, audit, renewal, warranty, insurance) — these meet or exceed our positions and should not be reopened.

*Prepared on the basis of the verified findings supplied. No position is stated beyond those findings.*"}
